label: conj:tetraplectic-sw-localisation-bridge
title: Combinatorial evaluation of tetraplectic matrix elements by $S_5$ localization
html:
In Seiberg–Witten theory [seiberg-witten1994b] the masses of BPS states and the binding matrix elements are integrals over a 4-manifold, and path integrals over instanton moduli localize [nekrasov2002] at fixed points classified by tuples of Young tableaux. The Bring cone is a 4-manifold whose invariant measure already resolves \mathcal{H} = L^2(M, \Omega) into components indexed by partitions of 5.

Conjecturally the two indexings are one indexing, so that a physical matrix element

  E \;=\; \int_M \psi_\lambda^{*}\, H\, \psi_\mu \,\Omega

may be evaluated combinatorially: by Schur's lemma the operator H is constant on each isotypic component, and the Wigner–Eckart theorem reduces the cross terms to Clebsch–Gordan data for S_5 — replacing the integral over the cone by a finite table.

If it held, this would be the bridge from the continuous tetraplectic integral to the discrete categorical data the knot-invariant machinery runs on, and it is the same kind of reduction the chapter's Seiberg–Witten arc performs downstream on the exceptional divisors. It is recorded as a conjecture: the identification of the localization index with the S_5 index is exactly what is missing, so the Wigner–Eckart step currently has nothing to act on.
heading: Conjecture
